model_decisions.why: The two gates Sonnet failed most ARE the grounding guarantee: verbatim means the quote is not in the passage, modal-fidelity means the item states as required what the standard recommends. The director's own read found the rest -- implausible distractors beside a sensible key. A cheaper writer whose characteristic failure is mis-quoting the source is not cheaper.
kept_from_the_experiment: --writer-model and --solver-model: a model change is a flag, not a code change.
Spend metered PER MODEL, so a mixed run cannot be priced at one rate.
The balanced-bracket truncation test (the old one was defeated by the nested options array).
model_decisions.not_pursued: The empty-response mode (9 of 37 Sonnet writer calls returned no text). Ruled: it only occurred on Sonnet, so it is not chased.
model_decisions.measured_and_notable: The director read the rejects as 'the key is far longer than the rest'. Measured, it is NOT a length effect: key-is-the-longest-option 44% on the 9 rejects against 50% on the 20 accepts, mean key/longest-rival 1.02 against 1.07. The existing length-cue rule correctly did not fire and no length rule would have caught these. The defect is distractor PLAUSIBILITY, which CLAUDE.md s13 already records as needing an SME rather than a gate.

spend_usd._NOT_RECOVERABLE: THE TRANSLATION STAGE. The spend happens on the run that makes the calls; the artifact is written by the run that writes the rows, which resumes from the checkpoint and legitimately spends $0. So every ISMSF-TRANSLATION-*.json records usd: 0 and the per-round translation cost is gone. 304 item-translations with no price on any of them. Three runs were observed live and are the only translation figures that exist: PROMPT-123 $0.7531 for 5 items, PROMPT-124 $0.2315 for 1, PROMPT-125 $0.8520 for 5. NOT extrapolated to the other 293: a rate times a count is an estimate, and this file does not carry estimates. FIXED for ISMS-IA: the checkpoint now carries usd_cumulative and the artifact carries spend.usd_round.
